title: Sandy Baltimore grateful for Paris education but not looking back | News | Official Site
text:
Sandy Baltimore grateful for Paris education but not looking back | News | Official Site | Chelsea Football Club 
 Sandy Baltimore discussed how Paris and Paris Saint-Germain helped shape her both as a footballer and a person, but is only looking to the future with Chelsea now as she prepares to face her former club in west London. 
 Chelsea Women continue our unbeaten UEFA Women’s Champions League campaign on Wednesday evening when we host Paris Saint-Germain at Plough Lane, looking to register our third win. 
 For Baltimore, it is a fixture which will have added significance. She is preparing to line up against Paris Saint-Germain as an opponent for the first time, having won the league and three cups with PSG, as well as reaching the Champions League final in 2017.
 The French international was born and raised in the Parisian suburbs and began her professional career with the club, spending nine years representing Paris Saint-Germain before moving to England to join Chelsea in 2024.
 ‘I grew up in Paris, I was born there, so I grew up with PSG. They were my first team and it was good over there,’ Baltimore tells us ahead of Wednesday’s Champions League showdown.
 ‘I learned a lot of things about football and me personally in Paris, about women, about growing up, about developing as a person. I started football in school with the boys, just playing football outside with some friends, just chill.
 ‘I was 15 years old when I joined PSG, I was with the Under-19s straight away. Then after I trained with the Under-19s, I joined the first team at 16 or 17.
 ‘When you want to grow up more, it was good I joined PSG when I was younger. Then after, you just work every day, you learn, because they are also good players there. So I learned a lot.
 ‘It was good when we won the league. I was so happy because it was my first trophy, because I’m from Paris and I played for PSG, and you have also your family, your friends. You have a lot of things, so you feel good after that.’
 That meant it was a big step for Baltimore when she took the chance to leave Paris and PSG behind for London and Chelsea, moving away from her home city and club for the first time. Although there have been challenges along the way, she insists it was not a difficult switch to make.
 ‘Honestly, at the beginning for me it wasn't difficult, because it was my objective to grow, to change, to take another opportunity to progress in my career and as a woman. So I was happy to come here.
 ‘The leagues in England and France are different, especially the intensity and physicality, so I think I learn a lot because Chelsea is a good team, we have good players. So you work every day and then I progress also. It's good.
 ‘This season, at the beginning, I didn't play too much. When you are a player, you're a little bit frustrated to not play, but I have a big mentality and I also work with a mentality coach, so he helped me a lot.
 ‘Also, I don't talk too much, but I work hard every day. I learn and I just keep going because I don't want to give up. I never give up. So for me, it's important to keep going, go forward and then just show your quality on the pitch.’
 Now, her focus is fully on the Blues and gaining another important three points in this season’s Champions League on Wednesday, which could potentially move us into first place in the standings, if results elsewhere go our way.
 Chelsea head into the match on a high, too, after going clear at the top of the Women’s Super League table with a 1-0 win over Manchester City at the weekend, courtesy of Baltimore’s stunning strike in first-half added time.
 ‘It was important because we know how the table looks, it’s really tight,’ she added. ‘So it was important for us to win this game because every week it's hard to win.
 ‘But we did and we were so happy. We stuck together and I scored and I tried to help the team, so I was happy. I think we go forward with more confidence, because last week against Man City we played well.
 ‘But I think it's different, because the Champions League is the Champions League. Everyone wants to win that. I think every team looks different when it’s the Champions League, so you have to prepare for that and you’ve got to be on your best game.’
